messages:
Priya: Heads-up — I have a repro for a KV-cache / page-table anomaly that shows up on long‑context workloads. Host pinned memory climbs steadily, then we see an evict waterfall and a huge PT-walk CPU spike on H100. Repro steps attached.
Alex: Hmm seen something vaguely similar on an A100 run last week but it was less dramatic. Any perf counters+trace?
Priya: Pushed a minimal reproduce script to the thread (below). Run with a long context (>500k tokens) and repeated generation.
Priya: ```bash
python tools/repro_kvcache.py --model open-llm-x --context 750000 --batch 4 --iters 120 --device h100
```
Diego: Can you paste the runtime.log tail? especially kvcache evict/alloc lines.
Priya: tail from a failing run: 
```
[2026-03-10 14:22:05] kvcache: allocate page id=0x7f8b2 size=65536 owner=kv-slot-123
[2026-03-10 14:22:05] kvcache: evict start count=1024 reason=low-gpu-mem
[2026-03-10 14:22:05] pagetable: create_fragment thin_count=2304 frag_bytes=14MB
[2026-03-10 14:22:06] kvcache: evict completed evicted=998 duration_ms=1250
[2026-03-10 14:22:06] host: pinned_mem 1.9GB -> 6.2GB
[2026-03-10 14:22:07] pagetable: pt-walk CPU=85% stalls=620
```
Jordan: That pt-walk CPU spike + pinned mem jump looks like repeated host DMA for page owners. Are we asynchronously serializing page meta on the host?
Priya: We suspected PT thin-fragmentation: lots of small page allocations that defeat coalescing, forcing many small DMA bursts and repeated PT-walks during cache lookups. Seems amplified when kernel-selection switches to tiled-kernel-v2 (commit runtime/select_kernel_v2).
Alex: Interesting — kernel selection could change access pattern for KV read kernels (different prefetch stride). If stride mismatches page tiling we may get more PT faulting.
Sam: @infra-bot can you confirm if the node in qpu1 had nvlink <-> host DMA issues around that window?
infra-bot: Checking logs for qpu1... found transient pci-e reconfig at 14:21:59, no error-level events. Scheduling a health-check job against the node now.
Diego: Quick mitigation idea: reduce continuous-batching window and enable pt_coalesce heuristic. Can we toggle at runtime?
Priya: Yes, there's a dynamic flag: ``--runtime-flags pt_coalesce=1 batch_window_ms=12``. With that the reproducer still shows growth but evict waterfall frequency drops.
Jordan: Can you post perf counters? breakdown of L2 misses, PCIe tx, host DMA bursts?
Priya: From perf sample (aggregated):
```
L2_read_miss: +42%
PCIe_tx_bytes/sec: +3.1GB/s
host_dma_ops/sec: +1200 (bursting in 800-1200 ops spikes)
page_table_walks/sec: +900
```
Alex: That host_dma_ops/sec seems high for small pages. Supports thin fragmentation theory. Do we have allocation histogram?
Priya: Yes — histogram shows many small allocations bunched at 64KB and 128KB. Combined they account for ~60% of active page count.
Diego: Root cause hypothesis: tiled-kernel-v2 changes KV read kernel's vector width so it requests smaller contiguous slices, causing allocator to carve many small pages instead of reusing larger slabs. Over longctx these accumulate because evict heuristics prefer LRU by slot, not by slab locality.
Jordan: Nice hypothesis. How about a repro comparing tiled-kernel-v1 vs v2 with same workload?
Priya: Ran that: v1 stable memory, no host pinned spikes. v2 reproduces the growth within ~40 minutes.
Sam: Could be a regression introduced by select_kernel_v2. Can we bisect kernel selector commits to isolate the change?
Priya: Starting a bisect job now. Also pushed a small patch to allocator to bias for slab coalescing (branch: kvcache/pt-coalesce-experiment). Diego will run stress.
Diego: Running stress on A100 + MI250 as well. Early note: MI250 shows similar pattern but the amplitude is smaller — likely because MI's DMA scheduler batches host transfers differently.
tracing-bot: Perf traces uploaded: https://redwood-internal/traces/4740001234/pt-thin-frag-20260310 (flamegraphs + kernel traces)
Alex: I'll dig into flamegraphs. If allocator patch reduces fragmentation we should see host_dma_ops/sec drop and fewer PT-walk spikes.
Priya: Action items: 1) finish bisect to identify regression commit (Priya) 2) run allocator coalesce experiment across H100/A100/MI250 (Diego) 3) add PT tracepoints around kvcache evict/alloc to correlate with kernel selection (Jordan) 4) infra to run repro on qpu1 after health-check (Sam/infra-bot).
Sam: noted and will run canary tomorrow morning. Please tag me if you need to escalate. :thumbsup:
Priya: Thanks all — will post bisect results and attach a minimal flamegraph diff once I have it.
Jordan: If coalesce helps we should consider a short-term runtime flag toggle for Dedicated customers until we land a proper fix.
Priya: Agreed. I'll draft a rollback-safe flag and add docs.
Alex: Thanks — ping me when bisect narrows to a couple commits and I'll help narrow the kernel change.
Priya: Closing loop here for now, will update thread when bisect finishes.
